what: Nothing can run off the daemon's loop unless a job owns it: a plane task is added to a job's request (Jobs::add needs self.jobs[id].request). So a request certificate's check, which is made before there is a job, can only use the loop's own effects (Stat, ReadAll): an output no stamp vouches for is hashed on the loop, an outside read no watch vouches for is hashed on the loop, and the library's fingerprint after a restart can only be taken by making the request a job first (1 job and 1 task where the bar is 0).
cost: gap B closed short of the bar; gap C not closed by three lanes in a row; after a restart every output and every outside file of a certificate is hashed on the loop
cause: the plane's unit of work is a job's task; the daemon has no work of its own
whys: why hashed on the loop: the check has no job and only a job has tasks
why no job: the check is what decides whether there is one
why only a job has tasks: Jobs::add routes a batch's completions by job id
why: the daemon was built as a server of jobs, with nothing it does for itself (a start-up look, a check)
class: work that belongs to the daemon, not to a request, has no owner and so lands on the loop or is bolted onto the first job
prevention: one plane request of the daemon's own, opened as it starts: its tasks (the library's look, a certificate check's hashes) complete to the loop with a typed value and no job
workaround: a request that comes before the library is looked at becomes a job of one stage and is checked when it is in (Jobs::certify_late)
fix: none yet: written as the next gap in docs/v2/plan/design/certificate.md, State, and /tmp/certificate6/next.md
